styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Old town, Arab quarter and colonial streets.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Rawon, sate and street stalls all day.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Independence sites and the old harbour.

stays.why: Central. Walk to Tunjungan Plaza mall and the old colonial streets; easy for taxis and buses.
Next to Gubeng train station and the airport bus; good for early departures to Malang or Bromo.
Old city core near the Arab quarter, Chinatown and the bridge; budget hotels and street food.
Quieter, greener south side with malls and family hotels; a short ride from the centre.

food: Try rawon (dark beef soup with keluak nut), served with rice and bean sprouts. A local favourite.
Sate kelapa and lontong balap are Surabaya classics. Look for busy warungs (small eateries) at lunch.
The Arab quarter near Ampel: try nasi kebuli and fresh bread from the bakeries.
Cheap eats: street stalls and food courts, roughly Rp 15,000–40,000 a plate. Check prices first.
Drink bottled water. Ice from busy cafés is usually fine; skip it at quiet roadside stalls if unsure.
more_time: Add a day for Malang: cooler hill town with colonial streets, about 2 hours by train or car.
Bromo sunrise trips leave at night from Surabaya; expect a long, cold, bumpy drive. Book ahead.
Swap a city afternoon for a mangrove and fishing-village stop on the east coast; check transport on the day.

recommend.why: One night covers the old town and the food; add a night if you want a Bromo or Malang side trip.

month_notes: Wettest month: about 29 rain days. Plan indoor sights and carry a rain jacket.
Still very wet, around 28 rain days. Short heavy afternoon showers are likely.
Wet again, about 29 rain days. Expect hot, humid days near 30°C.
Rain eases to about 24 days. Mornings are often clearer; go out early.
Much drier: about 12 rain days. A good month to walk the old town.
Dry season starts: about 10 rain days and highs near 31°C.
Driest month, about 5 rain days. Best time for outdoor sightseeing.
Very dry, about 2 rain days. Hot at 31°C; carry water and use shade.
Dry and hot: highs near 32°C with only about 4 rain days.
Hottest month, highs around 33°C. Start early and rest at midday.
Rain returns: about 21 rain days. Keep a flexible indoor plan.
Wettest again, about 28 rain days. Pack rain gear and expect delays.

climate_guide.summary: Tropical and hot all year, around 30–33°C by day. Rain is heavy from November to April and light from June to September.

items.title: Best time: June to September
items.text: Driest months, with only about 2–10 rain days. Good for walking and day trips.

items.title: Wet season: November to April
items.text: About 24–29 rain days a month. Showers are often short but heavy; plan indoor backups.

items.title: Hot every month
items.text: Highs stay near 30–33°C and lows near 24–25°C. October is the hottest month.

items.title: Humid all year
items.text: Expect muggy air, especially near the coast. Light, breathable clothes help.

items.title: Afternoon storms
items.text: In the wet season, storms often hit in the afternoon. Do outdoor sights in the morning.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes, a rain jacket or umbrella, sandals, sunscreen and mosquito repellent.

transit.best: Ride-hailing motorbike taxis (Gojek, Grab) for most trips; buses if you're saving money.

modes.text: No metro or tram. Commuter trains are very limited; don't plan around rail.
Suroboyo Bus and Trans Semanggi are air-conditioned, Rp 5,000, cashless only (QRIS or e-money card). Clean but waits run 15–30 min; track them on the GOBIS app.
Gojek, Grab and Maxim work well; use GoRide or GrabBike to beat traffic. Taxis are plentiful — check the meter (argo) is on. Green SM runs an electric fleet.
Possible, but traffic is heavy and parking is hard. Most visitors do better with ride apps.
Patchy. Sidewalks are inconsistent, so use ride apps for anything beyond a few blocks.
Cycle rickshaws are common. Agree a price first, around Rp 5,000–20,000.
Ferries leave from Tanjung Perak harbour. Check schedules on the day.
